questions.q: If y = cos(x<sup>2</sup>), then dy/dx equals:
questions.explanation: By the chain rule, d/dx cos(u) = −sin(u) · du/dx. Here u = x<sup>2</sup>, so du/dx = 2x and dy/dx = −2x sin(x<sup>2</sup>).

questions.q: The matrix | 3 x ; 2 4 | is singular when x equals:
questions.explanation: A matrix is singular when its determinant is zero. Here det = (3)(4) − (x)(2) = 12 − 2x = 0, so x = 6.

questions.q: If a = i + j and b = j + k, then |a × b| equals:
questions.explanation: a × b = (1, −1, 1), so its magnitude is √(1 + 1 + 1) = √3.

questions.q: The probability that a leap year has 53 Sundays is:
questions.explanation: A leap year has 366 days = 52 weeks and 2 extra consecutive days. Of the 7 possible pairs, two contain a Sunday, so the probability is 2/7.

questions.q: The value of ∫ from −a to a of x<sup>3</sup> dx is:
questions.explanation: x<sup>3</sup> is an odd function, and the integral of an odd function over a symmetric interval [−a, a] is 0.

faq.q: What topics does the CBSE Class 12 Maths 2002 paper cover?
faq.a: It follows the Class 12 syllabus of that year — differentiation and integration, matrices and determinants, vectors and three-dimensional geometry, differential equations and probability. The same core areas still dominate the board paper today.

faq.q: Is the 2002 paper still worth solving for the current board exam?
faq.a: Yes. The format has changed — today's paper adds MCQ and case-study sections — but the underlying concepts are the same. Older papers like 2002 offer clean, well-set questions that are ideal for building fundamentals before you switch to recent sample papers.

faq.q: How is a matrix shown to be singular?
faq.a: A square matrix is singular when its determinant equals zero, which means it has no inverse. To check, compute the determinant and set it to zero; any value that makes it vanish makes the matrix singular.

faq.q: What is the best way to revise using an old paper?
faq.a: Solve it in one timed sitting without notes, mark it against the answer key, then re-work only the questions you got wrong. That targeted second pass fixes weak spots far faster than re-reading solved answers.
